# Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-09-23 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Homogeneity is a distributional property, not a lack of individual quality: in the PNAS Nexus study LLMs matched or slightly beat humans on individual originality for two of three tasks, while population-level diversity was much lower. The Hivemind paper likewise finds comparable overall quality but poor calibration of LMs, reward models and LM judges on generations that draw differing idiosyncratic human preferences. (medium confidence) — https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/3/pgag042/8529001 · keywords: Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Scope limits on the homogeneity findings: the PNAS Nexus study covers only publicly hosted, aligned LLMs and three divergent-thinking tasks. The longitudinal study cannot separate distillation, shared training data or shared techniques, samples one response per model per prompt, and notes some Infinity-Chat prompts themselves request similar outputs. (medium confidence) — https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/3/pgag042/8529001 · keywords: Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19437

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] In a PNAS Nexus study of 22 LLMs and 102 humans, LLM response variability was lower than human variability on all three divergent-thinking tasks: Alternative Uses 0.459 vs 0.699, Forward Flow 0.518 vs 0.642, Divergent Association 0.632 vs 0.791 (p<0.01). LLM responses mirror other LLM responses more than humans mirror other humans. (medium confidence) — https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/3/pgag042/8529001 · keywords: Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Artificial Hivemind paper defines two effects: intra-model repetition (one model repeats similar outputs) and inter-model homogeneity (different models independently converge on similar ideas with minor phrasing variations). It uses Infinity-Chat, 26K real-world open-ended queries with 31,250 human annotations (25 annotators per example). (high confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954 · keywords: Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19437
- [statement] A longitudinal study of 68 models from 12 providers (March 2023 to July 2026) reports cross-family semantic distance falling over time: on the Alternate Uses Task from about 0.50 to below 0.40, and on Infinity-Chat100 from about 0.34 to just above 0.32. All 1,000 resampling iterations gave negative slopes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.19437 · keywords: Inter-model homogeneity in open-ended generation · also: https://academic.oup.com/pnasnexus/article/5/3/pgag042/8529001
- [statement] The Hivemind paper measures similarity with cosine similarity of OpenAI text-embedding-3-small embeddings; secondary summaries note this is sensitive to surface phrasing and could overstate homogeneity, though verbatim-overlap examples suggest it is not a pure artifact. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22954
